cim_eredeti: How to Restore Old Photos: Scan, Repair, Colorize and Print (2026)
szoveg_eredeti:
Restoring an old photo takes four steps: digitize the print, repair the damage, optionally add color, and upscale the result so it prints sharply. The repair step used to mean hours with a clone brush in Photoshop. Today an AI editing model does most of it in seconds. The scan you start from and the checks you do afterwards still decide whether the result looks like your grandmother or like a stranger.

This guide covers the whole workflow, with the settings that matter at each step. It uses Krea’s tools for the AI steps, but the scanning, diagnosis and print advice applies whatever software you use.

Looking for deleted photos on your phone instead? That is recovery, not restoration: check the Recently Deleted album in Google Photos or iCloud Photos first, since both keep deleted items for a limited time.

Left: the damaged print. Right: a Krea 3 restoration of it. The people, pose and black and white tones stay the same; the tears, creases and dust are gone.

The digital copy is what you restore. The print itself should leave the process exactly as it went in.

The scan sets the ceiling for everything that follows. AI repair recovers a lot, but it cannot see detail that the scan never captured.

Each kind of damage has a likely fix. Look at the scan at 100% zoom before you choose a tool.

Most old photos have several of these at once. Fix the damage first, then colorize, then upscale. Each step works best on a clean input.

Krea’s photo restoration tool runs Krea 3, Krea’s image editing model, with a restoration instruction already filled in. It removes scratches, creases, tears, stains and dust, recovers faded detail, and keeps the people, the pose, the framing and the original black and white or sepia tones.

A cracked 1920s sepia portrait, before and after Krea 3. The sepia tone is kept; only the damage is removed.

If you want more control, open Krea Edit and describe the repair yourself. Start from the instruction the restoration tool uses and adjust it:

Restore this old photo. Remove scratches, creases, tears, stains, and dust, and recover faded detail. Keep the same people, faces, pose, framing, and original tones.

Restoration fixes damage to the print. It does not fix a photo that was out of focus or shaken when it was taken. For that, use unblur image: it removes motion blur and soft focus and recovers fine detail in faces, text and textures, while the people, colors and composition stay the same.

A shaky storefront photo, before and after unblur. The blur is removed; the scene stays the same.

Once the photo is repaired, the photo colorizer turns black and white into realistic color. It reads skin, sky, foliage, clothing and materials and colors each one, instead of washing the whole image with one tint.

Colorize after you repair, not before. Scratches and stains confuse the colorizer, and repairing a colorized photo can shift the colors.

A restored photo often needs more pixels than the scan had, especially if you want to print it larger than the original. Print shops ask for about 300 pixels per inch for a sharp print, so:

A 2K restoration is enough for small prints. For an 8 × 10 or a framed enlargement, run the finished photo through the Krea Enhancer. It sharpens detail and increases resolution, and it works on old family photos as well as modern ones. You can try it free without an account, with a limited number of free enhancements. Paid plans upscale images up to 22K (pricing). Our roundup of AI image upscalers compares it with other options.

Upload a scan or a phone photo of the print. Krea 3 removes scratches, tears and stains in seconds with a free Krea account.

AI restoration covers most family photos: scratches, folds, stains, fading, small tears and missing corners. A professional photo restorer is still worth paying for when:

Professional restoration is usually quoted per photo, based on how much damage there is. Run the photo through an AI tool first: even if you then hire a professional, you will know which problems are easy and which are the hard part.
